sections.content: Every value has a type that decides what you can do with it. Numbers support math, strings support text operations, and booleans represent true/false.
Mixing types carelessly causes bugs — adding a number to text may concatenate or error depending on the language. Knowing your types prevents surprises.
Key points: common types are int, float, string, bool; some languages require declaring types, others guess them.

sections.codeExample:
name <- "Alice"
age <- 30
# Common types: "Alice" is a string, 42 is a number, TRUE is a boolean
